paper.title: Learning in Restless Bandits under Exogenous Global Markov Process

settings.name_in_paper: Restless multi-armed bandit under exogenous global Markov process
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Restless Markovian arms (environment markovian), declared out of scope in ontology v0.5
unmapped: An unknown exogenous global finite irreducible aperiodic Markov chain governs the arms' reward distributions; the global state is inferred after each play
Each arm's reward is a finite-state irreducible aperiodic Markov chain per global state, evolving regardless of actions (restless)
Regret is measured against a genie that knows the global transition probabilities and the arm means, and plays the arm with the highest one-step expected value V_s^i given the current global state
The learner knows an upper bound on Delta (the minimum squared gap of the values), plus the system constants used in I_L, I_G and L (eigenvalue gap, x_max, |X_max|, pi_hat_max, |S|, V*_max)
settings.definition_quote: We consider a set of $N$ arms, ... and a global system state process $\{s_t\}_{t=1,2,...}$, which is governed by a finite space, irreducible, and aperiodic discrete time Markov chain $\mathcal{S}$ with unknown transition matrix $P_S$. ... For each global state $s \in \mathcal{S}$, the $i^{th}$ arm is modeled as a finite space, irreducible, and aperiodic discrete time Markov chain $\mathcal{X}^i_s$ with unknown transition matrix $P_{\mathcal{X}_s^i}$.

algorithms.name: LEMP (Learning under Exogenous Markov Process)
requires_knowledge_of: Delta (upper bound on min squared value gap)

symbols.x_max: maximal reward state value over arms and global states
symbols.A_i: arm-dependent exploration constant: max{2/(eps^2 I_L), 2/(eps^2 I_G), max_s D_bar_{s,max}^i} if i in K_s for all s, else max{2/(eps^2 I_L), 2/(eps^2 I_G), 4L/Delta}
symbols.M_max_i: max over global states and state pairs of the mean hitting time for arm i
symbols.pi_min: minimal stationary probability of a local state
symbols.pi_s_max: max_s pi_s, maximal stationary probability of a global state
symbols.C_0: constant independent of t (the O(1) term, x_max E[T_1])

conditions: global chain and each arm's chain per global state are finite, irreducible and aperiodic
local state spaces of different global states are disjoint (global state recoverable)
an upper bound on Delta (the minimum squared value gap) is known
tuning: exploration thresholds use I_L, I_G and L as defined in (eq:I_L),(eq:I_G),(eq:L)

source.label: th:regret
source.quote: Assume that LEMP algorithm is implemented and the assumptions on the system model described in Section \ref{sec:problem} hold, and an upper bound on $\Delta$ in known. ... Then, the regret at time $t$ is upper bounded by: $\mathbb{E}_{\phi} [r(t)] \leq x_{\max} \cdot \bigg[\sum_{i=1}^N (\frac{1}{3} [4(3A_i\cdot \log(t)+1)-1] +M^i_{max} \cdot \log_4(3A_i\log(t)+1) ) +6 N |\mathcal{S}| (\frac{|\mathcal{S}||\mathcal{X}_{\max}|}{\pi_{\min}}+2|\mathcal{S}|) \max_s \pi_s \cdot \lceil \log_4(\frac{3}{2}t+1) \rceil \bigg] +O(1)$

results.notes: Paper's N (number of arms) mapped to K; t is the time index T. The O(1) term is represented as the declared constant C_0. Regret is defined as the expected sum of realized reward differences relative to the arm with the highest one-step expected value given the global state; recorded as dynamic_regret against the per-round best arm. Lemmas 3 and 4 (exploration and exploitation pull-count bounds) are its components and are not recorded separately. Overall order is O(log t).
